back: A style of programming that decides how a solution is described: low-level, imperative (procedural), object-oriented or declarative.
Close to the hardware (machine code, assembly); specific to one processor; direct control of registers and memory.
A program is a sequence of statements that change the program's state, organised in procedures and functions: how the result is obtained.
A program built from objects that combine data and methods, created from classes.
The programmer states what result is wanted (facts, rules, queries); the system decides how.
General-purpose: used for many tasks (Python, Java). Special-purpose: made for one task (SQL for databases).
Low-level: drivers, embedded controllers. Imperative: calculations and scripts. OOP: large systems, games, GUIs. Declarative: database queries, expert systems.
A language can support several paradigms (Python is imperative and object-oriented); a paradigm is a style, not a language.
Link a feature of the problem to the strength of the paradigm: hardware control, step-by-step processing, interacting objects, queries over facts.
